idiom_name: handler function + database/sql Tx with defer tx.Rollback()
implementation_notes: Go's grain is the pattern itself: an http.HandlerFunc (or a queue-worker function) is one procedure per request, and database/sql makes the transaction a first-class value. Begin with db.BeginTx(ctx, nil), defer tx.Rollback() immediately after a successful begin, run every statement through the Tx methods (tx.ExecContext/QueryRowContext - never the bare DB methods, which execute outside the transaction), and finish with tx.Commit(); after a successful commit the deferred rollback is a harmless no-op returning ErrTxDone. The thin gateway is the *sql.DB plus query helpers or sqlc-generated code, and because errors are returned values rather than exceptions, each step of the script is checked explicitly.
pitfalls: Mixing tx methods with db methods inside the same script splits the work outside the transaction without any error.
The context passed to BeginTx governs the transaction: a short client timeout cancels it mid-script and rolls the work back.
Treating the error from Commit as ignorable: a failed commit can leave the outcome unknown, and Go hands you the error rather than panicking.
